every snapshot's lamports match validator-observed pre/post balances

read-only accounts are byte-identical across the boundary; validator metadata records no account data, so their bytes rest on the archive and on V1 reproducing the original outcome

the Clock and StakeHistory sysvars are exempt from that byte-identity check: the runtime rewrites them every slot, so they carry no boundary evidence and are supplied to the replay at their acquired S-1 values

the reserve stake account is debited through the Stake program's Withdraw, which the runtime implements natively; its delegation state and the rent-exempt floor it must retain are enforced by that program, not by this adapter
supported contract is one WithdrawSol from a pool with no SOL withdraw authority, with cross-program invocation into the SPL Token and Stake programs only

the Clock and StakeHistory sysvars the withdrawal reads are acquired at the historical boundary like any other account; the Stake program's lockup and deactivation checks therefore see the slot's real values
the pool's own share arithmetic reads no Clock; the pinned replay clock reproduces the transaction's slot and block time
2 message key(s) held no account at either boundary and the validator recorded a zero balance for each; the runtime materializes them as empty System-owned accounts, matching the original execution
